Qitab-e-Noor
Your Spiritual Companion

Privacy Policy

Last updated 29 October 2026

Qitab-e-Noor keeps your worship record on your device. An account is optional and only stores what syncs — bookmarks, notes and similar saved items. There are no ads, no analytics trackers, and nothing is sold.

The short version

Most of what you do in this app — reading, prayer tracking, dhikr counts, journal entries, downloaded Quran — stays on your phone or tablet.

If you create an account, the items you choose to sync are stored on our server so they survive a new device. You can delete the account and everything attached to it from Settings at any time.

What stays on your device

These stay on your phone or tablet and are not uploaded anywhere:

  • Your name, prayer log, tasbih counts, good-deed record, journal reflections, bookmarks cache and reminder settings.
  • Community posts and comments, and E-Learning course progress. These are local-only by design.
  • Downloaded Quran translations, reciter audio and cached hadith or news, so the app works without a connection.
  • AI usage counts — how many answers came from live AI or the offline knowledge base. Only totals are kept; no question or answer text is stored with them.
  • Your app-lock PIN, stored in the operating system’s secure storage, never on our server.
  • Uninstalling the app removes this local data. Export a backup from Settings first if you want to keep it.

What an account stores on our server

If you sign in, the server stores your email address, your name, and a password hash produced by bcrypt. It never stores your password itself. The session token is kept in the device’s secure storage, not in ordinary app storage.

The server also stores the items you sync: bookmarks, notes, favourite duas, reminders, tasbih history, prayer toggles, good deeds, journal reflections, Khatm plans, and preferences such as theme, language, calculation method and a saved location if you set one.

Duas for where you are

The Duas screen can suggest a dua that fits your moment. The time of day, the day of the week and the chips you tap (mosque, home, market, travelling, rain, near water, mountains, dry spell, unwell, study, worried) are handled entirely on the device. The Islamic month and the moon phase are calculated from the clock alone.

If you tap “Use my location” or allow live context, the app asks for location permission and reads your position. To name a place such as “Central Masjid” or “Souq Road” it uses the geocoder built into your phone — Apple Maps on iOS, Google Play services on Android.

To suggest a dua for the weather or the landscape, the app sends only your coordinates — never your name, email or account — to Open-Meteo for the current conditions, the last 92 days of rainfall and the elevation, and to OpenStreetMap’s Overpass service for nearby rivers, lakes, peaks, woods and coastline. Those services answer with the sky and the landscape; the result is kept on your device and is not saved to your account. Tap Pause on the Duas card to stop live updates at any time.

Your coordinates are not sent to the Qitab-e-Noor server, are not saved to your account, and are not kept after the lookup. The chips offer the same suggestions without using location at all. The web preview cannot name places with the device geocoder, but weather and landscape context still work from the browser’s own location permission.

The AI assistant

When you ask the Islamic assistant a question, the app sends that question and up to three short entries from the app’s built-in knowledge base to our server. If a live model is configured, the server forwards that material to Anthropic, the provider of the Claude model, to produce an answer.

Your chat history is not sent to the server, and we do not store conversation transcripts. Anthropic processes the request under its own terms and privacy policy. Please do not type personal, medical or financial details into the assistant; it is a study companion, not a confidential service.

If no model is configured or the connection fails, the answer is produced entirely on your device from the offline knowledge base, and nothing leaves the phone.

Permissions the app may request

The app asks only for the permissions these features need:

  • Notifications, for prayer times, Quran reminders and daily dhikr. These are scheduled by the device. While the app is open, today’s reminders also appear on the main screens every five minutes; that card only reads the reminders saved on your device.
  • Approximate or precise location, for prayer times, the Qibla direction and the optional “dua for where you are” lookup described above. For prayer times and the Qibla it is used on the device; for the live dua context only the coordinates go to the weather and map services named below, never to our server. It is only saved to your account if you choose to save a location.
  • Motion and compass sensors, for the Qibla finder.
  • It does not request access to your contacts, photos, microphone, camera or files.

Third-party content services

Quran translations and recitations are fetched from the Quran.com API, hadith texts from a public content CDN, and Islamic news headlines from the publishers’ RSS feeds — including Al Jazeera, and occasionally through Google News when a publisher blocks our server. Those services receive the ordinary technical details of any web request, such as your IP address, but not your account details.

For the live dua context, Open-Meteo supplies weather and elevation, and OpenStreetMap’s Overpass service supplies the names of nearby rivers, lakes, peaks, woods and coastline. Both receive only the coordinates described above.

The weather shown on the Home dashboard and in the Duas card comes from Open-Meteo. The app sends the city name saved for prayer times, or — when the device has a GPS fix — your coordinates, so the reading matches the sky above you. It keeps the latest reading on the device for thirty minutes, so it can still be shown without a connection.

Sharing content

When you share a verse, dua or page through WhatsApp, Instagram, Copy Link or the system share sheet, the text and link are handed to the app you picked. We do not record what you share or with whom.

Security

Traffic between the app and the server uses HTTPS in production. Passwords are hashed, and tokens are stored in the operating system’s keystore or keychain. You can also set a PIN to lock the app.

No system is perfectly secure. The strongest protection for your account is a password you do not reuse elsewhere.

Keeping and deleting your data

Synced data is kept for as long as your account exists. Deleting the account from Settings asks for your password, then removes the account and every row attached to it immediately, including the synced items listed above. Personal data stored on that device is cleared at the same time.

Some backups you exported yourself, and data you shared with other people, are outside our control and are not removed by deleting the account.

Children

The app is not directed at children under 13, and an account requires an email address. Core reading and prayer features work without an account.

Changes and contact

If this policy changes in a way that affects what is collected, the in-app version and the published version are updated together, and the date at the top changes.

Questions about privacy can be sent to support@qitabe-noor.app.
